LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To give and follow simple directions and instructions.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.

•	 TR#4 What Do You Do?

BEFORE CLASS
Check the teacher’s dashboard to see if the Ss have completed 
at least half of the recommended activities up to this point.
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (12’)
•	 Hello + register + booklets 
•	 Moods version 2, TR#4 (optional)
•	 Calendar

2.– ACTIVITY 1: CHARACTER MATCHING (8’)
P.2.1
P.2.1
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the actions that each character is doing by 
putting the Place cards (P.2.1) down on the table. Say, “Grandpa 
and Grandma are going to the doctor’s, Mum is going to the 
hairdresser’s, and Dad is doing the gardening.”
Show the Ss the X cards and ask, “Why can’t Mum take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop?”, to which they should reply, 
“Because she is going to the hairdresser’s.” Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the pairs.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
To introduce the activity, say, “Let’s see if you remember 
what Pam and Paul’s family are doing!”. Put the P.2.1 cards 
in two piles face down: X cards on one side, Place cards on 
the other. The Ss must flip a card from each pile to match the 
character with the correct reason for them to not be able to 
take Pam and Paul to the toyshop.
If they have a match, they should say, “Mum can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop, because she is going to the 
hairdresser’s. I’ve got a pair!” If they don’t, they should say 
“I’ve got Grandpa and Grandma and doing the gardening; it’s 
not a pair, what a shame!”
> Correct matches and structures
•	 Mum + going to the hairdresser’s: “Mum (she) can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop because she is going to 
the hairdresser’s.” 
•	 Dad + doing the gardening: “Dad (he) can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop because he is doing the gardening.” 
•	 Grandma and Grandpa + going to the doctor’s: “Grandma 
and Grandpa (they) can’t take Pam and Paul to the 
toyshop because they are going to the doctor’s.”

> Follow-Up
Quickly split the group into two teams. Show team A the X 
card and team B the matching place card. Each team should 
say the part of the structure corresponding to their card. For 
example:
•	 Team A: “Grandpa and Grandma can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop...”
•	 Team B: “...because they are going to the doctor’s.”
3.– STUDENT STORYTELLING WITH CHANGES (PP.2-7) 
(10’)
Have your students choose new variables and tell the first half 
of the story themselves. Please see the section on storytelling 
in the Warm-Up Routines Index. 
4.– WORKSHEET: FOLLOWING DIRECTIONS (P.8) (8’)
Following Directions
8
NOTE: if you collected your Ss books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
MATERIALS
•	 Crayons or colouring pencils
Ss must follow your instructions and draw the path from 
one spot to another. 
Ask the Ss to take their crayons and place them on a start 
spot of your choice. Then begin to give them instructions to get to 
whichever spot you decide. The Ss must draw the path following 
your instructions and, when they get to their “destination”, they 
must circle it. Remember to use the expressions “turn left”, 
“turn right”, “go straight ahead” or “go past”. Once you are 
approaching your destination, tell them where it is by using 
the expressions “between”, “next to”, “in front of”, “behind”, 
“opposite”, “to your left” or “to your right”. You can follow

this model: “You are at the sports centre. When you exit the 
sports centre, turn left, and go past the charity shop. Go 
straight ahead and go past the clothes shop and the café. At 
the newsagent’s, turn right. Go straight ahead and turn right 
again. The shop you are looking for is opposite the pet shop 
(it’s the shoe shop).”
Do this activity two or three times depending on how much 
time you have. The students should use a different coloured 
crayon each time they follow new directions so they don’t get 
confused.
Once you have finished, ask a few Ss to repeat the instructions 
to you. Say, “I need to buy a courgette at the greengrocer’s. Can 
you tell me the way?” and have them repeat the instructions 
that you previously gave them.

> Scenario A
If your group has achieved the activity goal on My Way (i.e., 
they have done all or most of the activities in the current Mission),

say, “You’re doing amazing on My Way! You have played lots 
of games in Mission 2, so we can do a special sticker activity 
together!”. Take the Day 5 stickers and have them ask, “Can I 
have some stickers, please?”. Do the activity as instructed below. 
> Scenario B
If your group hasn’t reached the activity goal on My Way, 
simply move on with the class. You will have to complete one 
or two activities from the bonus section to make up for the 
time allotted to this dynamic.
The point of this activity is to review what you can buy at each 
shop in a fun way using the sticker pages. Ss have to stick the 
stickers depicting different items and answer the questions. 
Model the task with your Ss by looking for the stickers, sticking 
them, and answering the questions.
Have Ss open p.17 (sticker pages section) and say, “Let’s find 
out where we can buy these items!”. Point to square number 
eighteen and ask, “What number is this?”. Ss should respond, 
“It’s number 18!”. Say, “Can you find number 18 on the sticker 
sheet? What is it?”, and elicit, “Here it is! It’s a football!”. Have 
Ss place the sticker and ask them, “Can you buy football’s at 
the butcher’s?”, eliciting the response “No, you can’t!”
Continue in the same manner and stick as many stickers as 
time allows. We recommend making this activity more dynamic 
by making it a competition to answer the questions as fast 
as possible. You can give points to Ss who respond correctly.
If you can’t finish the whole page, tell the Ss that they can 
continue at home.
KEY (From top to bottom, left to right)
Sticker 18: Can you buy footballs at the butcher’s? No, 
you can’t!
Sticker 17: Can you buy trousers at the greengrocer’s? 
No, you can’t!
Sticker 20: Can you buy cereal at the clothes shop? No, 
you can’t!
Sticker 19: Can you buy croissants at the bakery? Yes, 
you can!
Sticker 22: Can you buy sandals at the shoe shop? Yes, 
you can!
Sticker 21: Can you buy lettuce at the newsagent’s? No, 
you can’t!
7.– ACTIVITY 4: FOLLOWING DIRECTIONS (5’)
> Warm-Up
Put a red sticker on each Ss’ left hand and a green one on 
their right. Then practise left, right and straight ahead by using

your hands. Say, “Turn left!” and have everybody turn to the left 
(you should too; having your back turned to your Ss is helpful, 
so everybody is pointing to the same left). Do the same with 
right and straight ahead.
Gradually say each command faster and faster.
> Main Activity
Next, the Ss should form a line. When you say, “Go straight 
ahead”, they must pat the person in front of them on the head. If 
you say, “Turn left” Ss must pat the left shoulder of the person 
in front of them and if you say, “Turn right”, their right shoulder. 
Finally, get them (still in a line) to follow your instructions 
but walking around the class pretending to be on a train.
> Advanced Groups
If your Ss have understood the concepts quickly, you can 
let them take on the teacher role and give commands to their 
classmates. 
8.– ACTIVITY 8: TAKE A WALK (VERSION 2) (TR#15) (5’)
P.2.5
> How to Play
This version of this activity is played like the musical chairs 
game.
Put up the Shop cards (P.2.5) that appear in Take a Walk 
Version 2 (TR#15) (pet shop, ice cream parlour, clothes shop, 
toyshop and bakery) around the room. Look at the lyrics and 
try not to place the shops that are sung one after another too 
close together.
> Warm-Up
If you feel it is necessary, quickly drill the names of the 
different shops or places.
To do this without taking the cards off the wall, walk around 
the room and ask Ss to shout out the different names saying, 
“It’s the clothes shop! It’s the bakery!” etc.

NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s take a walk around 
town!”. Next, play the song Take A Walk Version 2 (TR#15). 
Ss must sing along to the song and walk around the room and 
when they hear one of the shops or places being mentioned, 
they must go and point to that place.
During the musical interlude, encourage Ss to ask, “Where 
shall we go next?”
> Follow-Up
If time allows, ask each S, “What can you buy at the...?” 
and the Ss individually, each saying a different item, should 
say, “You can buy ... at the...”. Challenge them to come up with 
items they haven’t learned in class.

> How to Play
Each S will take a food cutout from a cloth bag and their 
classmates will help them to stick it on the Supermarket sheet 
(P.2.2) by giving them instructions on where to place it. 
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the prepositions using your hands: next to, 
between, behind, in front of and opposite. Then review the names 
of the different cutouts found in the cloth bag by asking, “What 
are these?/What is this?” and get the S to reply using a full 
structure, “They are cherries./It is a turkey!”. Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the food items.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Put all the activity cutouts in a cloth bag. Pair up the Ss (S1 and 
S2). Tell the Ss, “Let’s put the food items in the supermarket!”. 
To do the activity, proceed as follows:
•	 S1: Takes a food cutout. 
•	 S2: “What have you got?”
•	 S1: “I’ve got lettuce.”
•	 S2: “Where does the lettuce go?”
•	 S1: “The lettuce goes ....” and places the cutout on the 
correct spot using Blu-Tack.
> Follow-Up
To follow up, ask Ss where the different items are. For example, 
“Jane, where does the lettuce go?”, to which Jane will have to 
answer, “The lettuce goes next to the cherries.”

ACTIVITY 6: FREEZE!
P.2.5
> Main Activity
The Ss sit on the floor in a circle. Tell them, “Let’s see if you 
remember what you can buy at each shop!”. Place the pile of 
Shop cards (P.2.5) face down in the middle of the circle and 
get the Ss to begin passing the ball. Tell them that when you 
say “Freeze!”, they must stop. Whenever you feel like it, shout 
out “FREEZE!” and the S holding the ball must pick up a flash 
card from the middle of the circle and answer the question, 
“What can you buy at the…?” as quickly as possible. Once Ss 
are used to the game you can make it more dynamic by not 
asking them the question and letting them come up with the 
sentence themselves. For example:
•	 You can buy jumpers at the clothes shop.
•	 You can buy video games at the toy shop.
•	 You can buy muffins at the bakery.
NOTE: you can also play songs from the story to make it 
more dynamic. You can still say “Freeze!” every time you pause 
the song.
